classification_definitions.confirmed: Covers means of safe water supply and proper disposal of fluid waste, including complete removal of waste and maintenance/replacement of those items. Authority cited: B&P §§7008, 7059.

B&P §7057(b): a B contractor may not take a prime contract for trades other than framing/carpentry unless the contract requires at least two unrelated trades or the contractor holds the appropriate specialty classification or subcontracts with one. §7057(c): C-16 and C-57 require the specialty license.
Lays out and installs gypsum wallboard assemblies including nonstructural metal framing, and performs taping and texturing.

regulatory.confirmed_verbatim: "You need a permit before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes that will be covered by a wall or buried in the ground." Contractor licence types accepted: C4, C16, C20, C36, C54, B, A. Homeowner self-application limited to stand-alone single-family R-3 dwellings. Inspect before covering pipes. Contact: Permit Center help desk 628-652-4900, permitsf@sfgov.org.
"Minor repairs to existing interior plaster or wallboard, unless they are required for fire protection" is listed among interior work that does not need a permit.

§7048(a) exempts work where the aggregate contract price is less than $1,000, the work is casual/minor/inconsequential, and the work does not require a building permit. Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 12 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026.

"You need a permit before renovating and replacing kitchen or bath fixtures." Online eligibility: no wall removal or moving, R-3 or a unit in an R-2 building, and a legally permitted kitchen or bath. Only property owners and licensed B contractors may apply for the kitchen/bath permit; related electrical and plumbing permits are separate and skippable for B-only contractors only when tied to a kitchen/bath permit. Final inspections cannot be scheduled until related plumbing passes.
regulatory.note: New read added on 2026-11-10; the earlier ledger entry for S94 summarised only part of this page.

regulatory.confirmed_verbatim: B&P 7059(a): "Nothing contained in this section shall prohibit a specialty contractor from taking and executing a contract involving the use of two or more crafts or trades, if the performance of the work in the crafts or trades, other than in which they are licensed, is incidental and supplemental to the performance of the work in the craft for which the specialty contractor is licensed." Amended by Stats. 2024, Ch. 485, Sec. 6 (SB 1455), effective January 1, 2025.
regulatory.note: Read again 2026-11-10. The word 'incidental and supplemental' is not defined by the statute; applicability to a ceiling cut-and-patch is therefore left undetermined on the site.
